evidence.quote: Inflation is now much closer to the FOMC's 2 percent objective. I expect that we will continue to make progress toward that goal.
as risks to inflation have diminished and risks to employment have risen, these risks have been brought roughly into balance.
The good news is that the rise in unemployment has been limited and gradual, and the level of unemployment remains historically low. Even so, the cooling in the labor market is noticeable.
I will carefully watch incoming data, the evolving outlook, and the balance of risks when considering additional adjustments to the federal funds target range
To maintain the strength of the labor market, my FOMC colleagues and I recalibrated our policy stance last month, lowering our policy interest rate by 1/2 percentage point.

parsed.rationale: The speech is mostly about the discount window, but its brief outlook section describes easing inflation, a cooling labor market and roughly balanced risks after a 50bp cut. It mildly implies further adjustments, though only on a meeting-by-meeting, data-dependent basis, giving a modest dovish lean.
